newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ICE SEES DOUBLE-DIGIT GROWTH ON HUNGARY SHARE MKT.
newsitem.headline: ICE SEES DOUBLE-DIGIT GROWTH ON HUNGARY SHARE MKT.

text.p: The Hungarian share market has the potential to rise 20 percent by mid-1997, after an around 30 percent gain since the beginning of the year, ICE Securities said in a market research, dated January 28.

"While the BUX index has already gained some 30 percent in the new year, we are not calling that the top of the market yet, since we predict the market to grow at least by a further 20 percent by mid-year," ICE's analyst Rudi Voros said.
The BUX index reached its highest level of 5,499.74 points on January 28, after finishing 1996 at 4,134.31 points.

The analyst also said ICE beleived the Hungarian corporate sector will still remain highly attractive, especially in comparison with other markets in the region, with above-inflation earnings growth potential.
"We estimate an average earnings growth in excess of 30 percent for 1997, while the market is trading on a prospective price-earnings multiple of only 10," Voros said.
The Hungarian government expects the inflation to be around 17 percent in 1997.
The analyst said ICE continued to put its vote on export-oriented companies.
"We continue to favour export-oriented companies of the manufacturing sector in 1997 with a few exceptions, despite an anticipated pickup in domestic demand," Voros said.

Most analysts believe Hungary's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth will speed up in 1997 after an almost flat GDP growth last year, on the back of the recovery in domestic consumption and speeding up of investments.
Voros said that within exporter companies those selling onto east European markets had an edge.

"While many of these (manufacturing exporter) companies were successful in directing exports to western markets after the collapse of the COMECON, they are now re-discovering their traditional markets in the neighbouring...region where economic growth is the highest in Europe," Voros said.
